newsitem.title: UK: Brazil oil product demand seen up 900k bpd by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oil product demand seen up 900k bpd by 2005.

text.p: Brazilian demand for refined oil products is set to grow by 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the year 2005, to 2.4 million bpd, an official said on Tuesday.

Luis Costa Milan, senior advisor to the chairman of state owned Petrobras, told the annual Centre for Global Energy Studies conference that demand for petroleum products in Brazil would grow by 4.7 percent per annum from a level of 1.5 million bpd in 1996.
Demand for natural gas would accelerate even faster, growing by 20 percent per annum during the same period, he said.
Natural gas's share of Brazil's primary energy consumption would jump from three percent in 1996 to eight percent in 2005.

Petrobras, which produced 900,000 bpd of oil in 1996 and 170,000 bpd of oil equivalent in natural gas, was currently building 11 new floating production facilities with an installed capacity of one million bpd which it expected to be operating in the next three to four years.
